flawed_step: Step 2: A proof cannot infer that a connected 3-regular graph is bridgeless, so Petersen's bridgeless theorem cannot be applied.
counterexample: Take three disjoint copies of K4, subdivide one edge in each copy with a new vertex x_i, and add a new vertex v adjacent to x_1,x_2,x_3. The resulting graph is finite, simple, connected, and 3-regular. Each edge vx_i is the sole edge joining a five-vertex lobe to the rest, so every perfect matching would have to contain all three edges vx_i. That is impossible because they share v.
assessment_summary: The bridgeless hypothesis cannot be dropped. The explicit connected cubic graph above has no perfect matching.
